perplexity.description:
Tommy (Original Soundtrack Recording) is a double album released in 1975 by The Who, accompanying the film adaptation of their 1969 rock opera. The soundtrack features a substantially reworked version of the original concept album, with Pete Townshend's synthesizer work and elaborate choral arrangements taking prominence throughout. Several tracks were radically reimagined by an all-star band for the film, while new compositions like "Champagne" and "Mother and Son" were created specifically for the soundtrack. John Entwistle contributed bass work and horn parts, while Kenney Jones handled drumming duties on many tracks.

The album represents a significant departure from the original rock opera in its orchestration and production approach, designed to accommodate the vocal performances of the film's actors rather than relying solely on the band's own vocals. The soundtrack spans 24 tracks across two vinyl records, progressing through the narrative arc of Tommy's journey from birth through his emergence as a messianic figure. The production showcases Townshend's ambitious vision for adapting the stage work to cinema, blending rock instrumentation with theatrical arrangements to support the film's visual storytelling.

The Tommy soundtrack established itself as a significant entry in the rock-opera film canon, demonstrating The Who's ability to reimagine their material for different media while maintaining the conceptual integrity of the original work. The album's release on Polydor Records in 1975 solidified the project's commercial reach, and it has since been reissued multiple times across various formats, including remastered CD editions and recent vinyl reissues, reflecting its enduring place in the band's catalog.
